item.title: EU considers response to Leipzig drone attack after Germany formally blames Moscow – Europe live
item.description:
Germany has accused Russia of carrying out a failed drone sabotage operation at Leipzig/Halle Airport and announced Tuesday it would close Russian diplomatic facilities, escalating tensions after investigators linked Moscow to last month's attack. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Russia's consulate in Bonn will be closed and the contract for the Russian House cultural center in Berlin will be terminated after German authorities concluded Moscow was behind the Aug. 4 incident. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said forensic evidence and intelligence findings tied Russia to the attack, in which authorities found a drone carrying an explosive device beside a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport. item.title: Nepal floods: Families gather at overwhelmed morgues in desperate search for loved ones
item.description:
In Nepal, the hope of finding survivors is fading daily. Bodies are piling up in morgues, and storage capacity is reaching its limit. Authorities are beginning to bury the remains after DNA samples are taken and an identification number is assigned. The hope is that families will be able to find them later. For the relatives of the missing, the wait is unbearable. They go from one hospital to another, consult the lists of survivors and scrutinise the photos of unidentified bodies. France 24's special correspondents met with several of these families at the morgue of Kathmandu University Hospital.

item.title: Global bond sell-off intensifies as US-Iran tensions stoke inflation fears
item.description:
Global bond yields hit their highest levels for decades over concerns about inflation, debt burdens, and central banks raising interest rates. Renewed conflict in the Gulf pushed oil prices up, and the US Federal Reserve chair made hawkish noises last week, while borrowing levels across the rich world look unlikely to abate anytime soon. Japanese 10-year bonds typify the surge, with yields hitting 3% for the first time since 1996 . Tokyo is planning a huge economic stimulus and greatly increased defense spending, alongside reduced tax cuts, fueling fears about Japan’s fiscal stability, while inflation has accelerated. But “ the bond sell-off has been a global affair ,” Deutsche Bank analysts told investors. — Tom Chivers

item.title: Alex Eala cruises into US Open second round, top seed Zverev survives
item.description:
German scrapes home 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7), 7-5, 6-4 in thriller ‘I think this is the longest first-round match I’ve played’ Alexander Zverev rallied just in time to avoid becoming the first men’s No 1 seed to lose in the first round of a grand slam tournament since 2003, edging Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7), 7-5, 6-4 in a US Open match that ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Zverev couldn’t cash in on repeated chances to break Sonego’s serve for much of the night and was in danger of becoming the first top-seeded man to fall in his first match in a major since Ivo Karlovic beat Lleyton Hewitt at Wimbledon in 2003. item.title: ‘Really terrified’: Milo Yiannopoulos speaks out after deportation from US
item.description:
Before last week , Milo Yiannopoulos was one of the most noxious, divisive, and broadly unpopular far-right figures in the country, having whittled down his allies in the movement over the past decade with a combination of exuberant misogyny and bigotry, catty infighting, an infamous moment of pedophilia apologism, and increasingly pointed criticism of Donald Trump. Now, he’ll have to settle for being a broadly divisive and unpopular figure in the UK, having been swiftly and very publicly deported back to his home country on Friday after being arrested at the New Orleans airport. item.title: Why a bill to juice condo construction died even though California lawmakers voted for it
item.description:
In summary Supporters said a condo construction bill was a key to unlocking the type of naturally affordable for-sale housing that California desperately needs. But deadlines matter. A bill that supporters hoped would kickstart California’s moribund condo industry and boost the scarce number of entry-level homeownership opportunities, died under mysterious circumstances at the stroke of midnight on Tuesday after failing to get a final vote before the end of the legislative session. Assembly Bill 1903 by Oakland Democratic lawmaker Buffy Wicks would have changed the way that disputes between homeowners and builders over purportedly shoddy construction are resolved in a way the bill’s author hoped would result in fewer defect lawsuits and less developer skittishness around building condos. .
